newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Konsortium says eyes minor stake in port.
newsitem.headline: Konsortium says eyes minor stake in port.

text.p: Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd chairman Mirzan Mahathir said on Tuesday he wanted to participate in a privatised local port, but without taking up a majority stake.
"I am not there to try to take equity position (majority stake) as it does not make sense," the national Bernama news agency quoted Mirzan as saying with reference to Westport Holdings.
"Equity position means huge responsibility, having to put in your own management and control," Mirzan told reporters, adding a minority stake would be sufficient.
Mirzan has said previously he was interested in acquiring a stake in Westport, operator of the new West Port container centre flanking Malaysia's premier shipping gateway of Port Klang.

"If Konsortium Perkapalan can have a say in the company or able to have an understanding of its operation in more detail without control of Westport Holdings, equity involvement would not be necessary at all," said Mirzan, eldest son of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
Container haulage and shipping firm Konsortium is building a goods distribution park in the West Port.
